name: Spherical Ceva Generalization to Non-Euclidean Spaces

insights: The weight-parameter framework extends identically to hyperbolic geometry
sinh(d(B,D))/sinh(d(D,C)) = β/α — same cancellation as spherical sin case
The key identity: (α+βm)² - n² = β²(m²-1) for hyperbolic (m>1), vs β²(1-m²) for spherical (|m|<1)
The √(m²-1)/n or √(1-m²)/n factor always cancels in the ratio, giving β/α
The concurrency criterion αD·αE·αF = βD·βE·βF is universal — works for Euclidean, spherical, and hyperbolic
The criterion is purely algebraic: it depends only on the weight parameters, not the geometry
